feedback.problem: A particle moves from the origin with an acceleration of $(-i+3j)\,{\text{cm/s}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $(4i+j)\,\text{cm/s}.$ Find the position vector of the particle after $2$ seconds.
feedback.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $a,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut+\frac{1}{2}a{t}^{2},
$$

 

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle and $u$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=0i+0j,\,u=4i+j,\,a=-i+3j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t=2\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(0i+0j)+(4i+j)(2)+\frac{1}{2}(-i+3j)(2)^{2} \\  & =(8i+2j)+2(-i+3j) \\  & =(8i+2j)+(-2i+6j) \\  & =(6i+8j)\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$
